finishes.note: Whole oval floor and the passage floor to the port face; voids filled (tinted cement); vein-cut bands along x (the direction of travel). Classical floors are honed, not polished (Palette verdict).
Two flush discs r 0.40 at (±7.20, 0); voids filled.
Flush ring r 0.40–0.45 round each viewing stone: oil-gilt on cast bronze, worn through to the brown bronze where stood on (Story: viewing-stone rings).
Oval inner face 0–5.00: lime plaster trowelled and burnished (marmorino), the one pale room; the willows hang on it.
P10 skirting, 0.10 high, 18 mm proud; voids open.
P9 cove, run in lime gauged with plaster of Paris, then burnished like the walls.
P6 slim architrave round the door on the oval face (the doorway surround is honed in every era).
Jambs and arched soffit of the passage from the port face to the oval's inner face; voids open.
Linen velarium, translucent, in 1.40 m widths along x with double-stitched seams; stretched on the bronze frame under the glass dome.
Rim ring and eight ribs above the seam lines carrying the cloth; hidden above the cloth, seen only as soft shadows in daylight.
Attic wall at the rim line, 6.35–7.20, facing the attic; white so the attic returns light onto the cloth.
Elliptic glass dome over the velarium: Optiwhite laminated with a UV-filtering interlayer, acid-etched on the inner face (the laylight). Glazed opening nympheas.roof, weather giverny.
Glazing bars 40 × 70 mm on a 1.20 m plan grid and the dome's curb, as the Salon's lantern frames.
Outer face of the oval wall (to 7.20) and the passage block's sides and top (5.20): honed ashlar, weathered (outdoors).
Roof ring 7.00–7.20 from the outer face to the rim line: milled sheet lead on boarding, laid with rolls.
Moulded sitting-height coping, 16 blocks; voids filled; hand and seat contact; a faint waterline under the lip (history to add in Matter).
Carved lily frieze on the die, from a close-grained filled block (voids filled, figure quieter); carved then honed.
Inner lip, one jointless ring carrying the line of warm light: oil-gilt on cast bronze, wetted at the waterline, worn through where hands rest.
Lining, bed and the two planting shelves: Belgian bluestone, honed, permanently submerged; the dark bed that makes the water a mirror.
Brimming still water dyed black with a reflecting-pool dye; mirrors the velarium and the panels.
Bronze tray under the whole pond out to the toe; the quiet bronze soffit seen from the stair when the pond is up.
Four telescopic posts (three stages each); statuary patina relieved bright where the stages slide.
The golden iris: a cast Iris laevigata at life size, oil-gilt, set on the coping's seat at the west apex; the gold worn through on the falls where it is touched.
The three retracting guard rails round the pond opening (M-2), rails and stanchions.
Curved oak seat slabs of the four benches, quartersawn, grain along the arc.
Two plinths under each seat; voids filled.
36 treads, risers and nosings (one stone per tread), the top and bottom landings; voids filled.
Closed strings on both walls and the 0.15 skirting on the bottom landing.
0.30 curb lining the opening's north, south and east edges and the slab edge; voids filled.

finishes.working: hand-laid, lime mortar, joints slightly recessed
finishes.note: Shaft side walls, west end wall and the head wall with the port's arched opening: the Reserve's brick (Palette: the long stair's shaft).
Soffit of the oval slab over the shaft, z −0.40, from the slab edge to the head wall.
Two handrails with brackets and wall roses; the patina relieved bright along the top where hands run.
On the stand only: closed pair of bronze doors in the east port's opening until salon.west is mated.
The Reserve's closed bronze doors: a closed pair in the stair port's arched opening, the port's blind while the Reserve is not built.
